claim: In the two-dimensional grand canonical Monte Carlo model of Fang, Hagan and Rogers -- a binary mixture with a short-ranged attractive well and no A-A binding, fed from a reservoir at 0.5% area fraction -- crystals with strong unlike binding E_AB form a square lattice with checkerboard order while the like binding E_BB is weak, and form hexagonal crystals (with stripe, then honeycomb, then demixed compositional order) once E_BB exceeds 1.2 kT.

numbers.name: pair_well_depth
numbers.note: E_BB, the B-B well depth above which the simulated crystals are hexagonal; the paper defines each E_ij as the depth of the pair-potential minimum.

validity_conditions: A MODEL RESULT, NOT A MEASUREMENT ON COLLOIDS. Two dimensions; grand canonical Monte Carlo with the authors' own C++ code, not HOOMD; periodic box 53.3 x 53.3 particle diameters; the pair potential is Rogers and Crocker's measured DNA-hybridisation potential with its range rescaled to about 5% of the diameter; A-A pairs never bind (E_AA = 0); reservoir at 0.5% area fraction with equal chemical potentials for A and B; insertion/deletion and species-flip moves once per 1,000 displacements on average; at least 2e10 displacement trials per run; no hydrodynamics. The 1.2 kT threshold is the one number the text gives for the simulated phase diagram (Fig. 3); how the boundary depends on E_AB is shown only in the figure and is not asserted here. A well depth in kT cannot bound a query condition in this store (kT needs a temperature to convert), so the threshold is carried in numbers and not in validity; validity holds the one convertible condition, the reservoir density.
